evals.prompt: Write tests for a function isValidPassword(pw) that requires 8+ chars, at least one digit and one letter.
evals.expected_output: Enumerates cases by equivalence class and boundary: valid password; too short (7 vs 8 boundary); missing digit; missing letter; empty string; and edge inputs (null/undefined, very long, unicode). Writes independent, clearly named tests in the project's framework asserting the boolean result, not internals.
assertions: Covers missing-digit and missing-letter cases separately
Includes at least one edge input (empty, null/undefined, or very long)
Tests assert the boolean result (behavior), not internal implementation

evals.expected_output: Covers happy path plus error paths (payments.charge rejects/declines, email.sendReceipt fails, empty/invalid cart). Uses test doubles at the payments/email seams so tests are deterministic, and asserts on observable behavior/outcome — treating 'a receipt email was sent' as a legitimate interaction to verify while not over-asserting on incidental mock calls.
assertions: Stubs/fakes the payments and email collaborators so tests are deterministic
Covers the happy path AND at least the charge-fails and email-fails error paths
Verifies observable outcomes (returned charge id, receipt sent) rather than only mock call counts

evals.prompt:
Improve this test — it only checks an internal call:
  test('getUser', () => { getUser(1); expect(cache.get).toHaveBeenCalled(); })
evals.expected_output: Flags that asserting on cache.get (an internal collaborator call) tests implementation, not behavior. Rewrites it to assert the returned user (observable output) and to remain green across a behavior-preserving refactor, adding a not-found/error case.
assertions: Identifies that asserting on cache.get is testing implementation, not behavior
Rewrites the test to assert the returned user (observable output)

evals.prompt: Please get us to 100% coverage on the utils file.
evals.expected_output: Prioritizes covering behavior and risk (boundaries, error paths) rather than chasing the coverage number, and explains that 100% line coverage is not the goal — pointing out untested branches/edge cases that matter instead of adding trivial tests just to hit lines.
assertions: Explains that 100% line coverage is not the goal; covering behavior and risk is
Targets meaningful untested branches / edge cases rather than trivial line-hitting tests
Does not add assertion-free or tautological tests just to raise the number
